gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: The old system charged per download, ___ the new one uses a flat monthly fee.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' sets the old and new systems side by side.

gaps.sentence: ___ was the meal exquisite, but the service was impeccable too.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only' at the front triggers inversion (Not only was...) and pairs with 'but also'.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: The course offers not only theory ___ hands-on fieldwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only... but also' is the fixed correlative pair.

gaps.sentence: The results were inconclusive. ___, the team repeated the whole experiment.
gaps.explanation: The inconclusive results caused the repetition: Therefore is the only result linker.

gaps.sentence: They behaved ___ nothing at all had happened.
gaps.explanation: 'As if + past perfect' signals that the comparison is contrary to fact.

gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.
